statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: To allow local policy changes to have the correct effect without resetting any BGP connections, a BGP speaker SHOULD either (a) retain the current version of the routes advertised to it by all of its peers for the duration of the connection, or (b) make use of the Route Refresh extension [RFC2918].
actions: retain current version of routes advertised by all peers for duration of connection
OR invoke Route Refresh extension per RFC2918

statements.subject: message
statements.description: KEEPALIVE messages may be sent periodically to ensure that the connection is live.
actions: send KEEPALIVE message to peer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a BGP speaker chooses to advertise a previously received route, it MAY add to, or modify, the path attributes of the route before advertising it to a peer.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The next hop for each of these routes MUST be resolvable via the local BGP speaker's Routing Table.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All implementations are required to support this maximum message size.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The smallest message that may be sent consists of a BGP header without a data portion (19 octets).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This 16-octet field is included for compatibility; it MUST be set to all ones.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The value of the Length field MUST always be at least 19 and no greater than 4096, and MAY be further constrained, depending on the message type.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Therefore, the Length field MUST have the smallest value required, given the rest of the message.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Upon receipt of an OPEN message, a BGP speaker MUST calculate the value of the Hold Timer by using the smaller of its configured Hold Time and the Hold Time received in the OPEN message.
actions: calculate Hold Timer as min(configured Hold Time, received Hold Time in OPEN message)

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The Hold Time MUST be either zero or at least three seconds.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An implementation MAY reject connections on the basis of the Hold Time.
actions: reject connection

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An UPDATE message MAY simultaneously advertise a feasible route and withdraw multiple unfeasible routes from service.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For well-known attributes, the Transitive bit MUST be set to 1.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For well-known attributes and for optional non-transitive attributes, the Partial bit MUST be set to 0.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when received.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This is a well-known mandatory attribute that defines the (unicast) IP address of the router that SHOULD be used as the next hop to the destinations listed in the Network Layer Reachability Information field of the UPDATE message.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The value of this attribute MAY be used by a BGP speaker's Decision Process to discriminate among multiple entry points to a neighboring autonomous system.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: This SHOULD be the same address as the one used for the BGP Identifier of the speaker.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An UPDATE message SHOULD NOT include the same address prefix in the WITHDRAWN ROUTES and Network Layer Reachability Information fields.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: However, a BGP speaker MUST be able to process UPDATE messages in this form.
actions: accept and process UPDATE message containing same address prefix in both WITHDRAWN ROUTES and NLRI fields

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker SHOULD treat an UPDATE message of this form as though the WITHDRAWN ROUTES do not contain the address prefix.
actions: treat WITHDRAWN ROUTES as not containing the duplicate address prefix when prefix also appears in NLRI

statements.subject: message
statements.description: KEEPALIVE messages MUST NOT be sent more frequently than one per second.
actions: Enforce minimum one-second interval between successive KEEPALIVE transmissions

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation MAY adjust the rate at which it sends KEEPALIVE messages as a function of the Hold Time interval.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If the negotiated Hold Time interval is zero, then periodic KEEPALIVE messages MUST NOT be sent.
actions: Disable periodic KEEPALIVE message transmission when negotiated Hold Time is zero

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: BGP implementations MUST recognize all well-known attributes.
actions: recognize all well-known attributes

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Some of these attributes are mandatory and MUST be included in every UPDATE message that contains NLRI.
actions: include mandatory well-known attributes in UPDATE message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Others are discretionary and MAY or MAY NOT be sent in a particular UPDATE message.

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: Once a BGP peer has updated any well-known attributes, it MUST pass these attributes to its peers in any updates it transmits.
actions: pass updated well-known attributes to peers in all transmitted updates

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: In addition to well-known attributes, each path MAY contain one or more optional attributes.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Paths with unrecognized transitive optional attributes SHOULD be accepted.
statements.trigger: receive UPDATE message with unrecognized transitive optional attribute
statements.pre_cond: attribute.optional = true & attribute.transitive = true & attribute.recognized = false
actions: accept path carrying unrecognized transitive optional attribute

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a path with an unrecognized transitive optional attribute is accepted and passed to other BGP peers, then the unrecognized transitive optional attribute of that path MUST be passed, along with the path, to other BGP peers with the Partial bit in the Attribute Flags octet set to 1.
statements.trigger: forward path with unrecognized transitive optional attribute to peers
statements.pre_cond: attribute.optional = true & attribute.transitive = true & attribute.recognized = false & path.accepted = true & path.forwarded = true
actions: pass unrecognized transitive optional attribute along with the path to other BGP peers
set Partial bit in Attribute Flags octet to 1

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a path with a recognized, transitive optional attribute is accepted and passed along to other BGP peers and the Partial bit in the Attribute Flags octet is set to 1 by some previous AS, it MUST NOT be set back to 0 by the current AS.
statements.trigger: forward path with recognized transitive optional attribute carrying Partial bit = 1
statements.pre_cond: attribute.optional = true & attribute.transitive = true & attribute.recognized = true & path.accepted = true & path.forwarded = true & attribute.partial_bit = 1
actions: preserve Partial bit at value 1; do not reset Partial bit to 0

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Unrecognized non-transitive optional attributes MUST be quietly ignored and not passed along to other BGP peers.
statements.trigger: receive UPDATE message with unrecognized non-transitive optional attribute
statements.pre_cond: attribute.optional = true & attribute.transitive = false & attribute.recognized = false
actions: silently ignore unrecognized non-transitive optional attribute
do not forward unrecognized non-transitive optional attribute to other BGP peers

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: New, transitive optional attributes MAY be attached to the path by the originator or by any other BGP speaker in the path.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All optional attributes (both transitive and non-transitive), MAY be updated (if appropriate) by BGP speakers in the path.

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The sender of an UPDATE message SHOULD order path attributes within the UPDATE message in ascending order of attribute type.
actions: order path attributes within UPDATE message in ascending order of attribute type

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The receiver of an UPDATE message MUST be prepared to handle path attributes within UPDATE messages that are out of order.
statements.trigger: receive UPDATE message with out-of-order path attributes
actions: accept and process path attributes that appear out of order in received UPDATE messages

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The mandatory category refers to an attribute that MUST be present in both IBGP and EBGP exchanges if NLRI are contained in the UPDATE message.
actions: include mandatory attributes in IBGP UPDATE messages containing NLRI
include mandatory attributes in EBGP UPDATE messages containing NLRI

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Its value SHOULD NOT be changed by any other speaker.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When a given BGP speaker advertises the route to an internal peer, the advertising speaker SHALL NOT modify the AS_PATH attribute associated with the route.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the act of prepending will cause an overflow in the AS_PATH segment (i.e., more than 255 ASes), it SHOULD prepend a new segment of type AS_SEQUENCE and prepend its own AS number to this new segment.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Whenever the modification of the AS_PATH attribute calls for including or prepending the AS number of the local system, the local system MAY include/prepend more than one instance of its own AS number in the AS_PATH attribute.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The NEXT_HOP is a well-known mandatory attribute that defines the IP address of the router that SHOULD be used as the next hop to the destinations listed in the UPDATE message.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When sending a message to an internal peer, if the route is not locally originated, the BGP speaker SHOULD NOT modify the NEXT_HOP attribute unless it has been explicitly configured to announce its own IP address as the NEXT_HOP.
actions: do not modify NEXT_HOP attribute

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When announcing a locally-originated route to an internal peer, the BGP speaker SHOULD use the interface address of the router through which the announced network is reachable for the speaker as the NEXT_HOP.
statements.trigger: announce locally-originated route to internal peer
actions: set NEXT_HOP to interface address of router through which announced network is reachable for the speaker

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the route is directly connected to the speaker, or if the interface address of the router through which the announced network is reachable for the speaker is the internal peer's address, then the BGP speaker SHOULD use its own IP address for the NEXT_HOP attribute (the address of the interface that is used to reach the peer).
actions: set NEXT_HOP to speaker's own IP address (address of interface used to reach peer)

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Otherwise, if the external peer to which the route is being advertised shares a common subnet with one of the interfaces of the announcing BGP speaker, the speaker MAY use the IP address associated with such an interface in the NEXT_HOP attribute.
statements.trigger: send UPDATE to external peer one hop away
actions: optionally set NEXT_HOP to IP address of speaker interface sharing common subnet with peer X

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: By default (if none of the above conditions apply), the BGP speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the interface that the speaker uses to establish the BGP connection to peer X in the NEXT_HOP attribute.
statements.trigger: send UPDATE to external peer X one hop away
actions: set NEXT_HOP to IP address of interface used to establish BGP connection to peer X

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The speaker MAY be configured to propagate the NEXT_HOP attribute.
statements.trigger: send UPDATE to multihop external peer X
actions: propagate NEXT_HOP attribute unchanged from learned route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: By default, the BGP speaker SHOULD use the IP address of the interface that the speaker uses in the NEXT_HOP attribute to establish the BGP connection to peer X.
statements.trigger: send UPDATE to multihop external peer X
actions: set NEXT_HOP to IP address of interface used to establish BGP connection to peer X

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker MUST be able to support the disabling advertisement of third party NEXT_HOP attributes in order to handle imperfectly bridged media.
actions: support configuration option to disable advertisement of third party NEXT_HOP attributes

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A route originated by a BGP speaker SHALL NOT be advertised to a peer using an address of that peer as NEXT_HOP.
actions: do not set NEXT_HOP attribute to peer's own address

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker SHALL NOT install a route with itself as the next hop.
actions: do not install route whose next hop resolves to speaker's own address

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The NEXT_HOP attribute is used by the BGP speaker to determine the actual outbound interface and immediate next-hop address that SHOULD be used to forward transit packets to the associated destinations.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the entry specifies an attached subnet, but does not specify a next-hop address, then the address in the NEXT_HOP attribute SHOULD be used as the immediate next-hop address.
actions: use NEXT_HOP attribute address as immediate next-hop address

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the entry also specifies the next-hop address, this address SHOULD be used as the immediate next-hop address for packet forwarding.
actions: use routing entry's next-hop address as immediate next-hop address for packet forwarding

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All other factors being equal, the exit point with the lower metric SHOULD be preferred.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If received over EBGP, the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute MAY be propagated over IBGP to other BGP speakers within the same AS (see also 9.1.2.2).
actions: propagate MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute over IBGP to BGP speakers within same AS

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute received from a neighboring AS MUST NOT be propagated to other neighboring ASes.
actions: do not propagate MULTI_EXIT_DISC to other neighboring ASes

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker MUST implement a mechanism (based on local configuration) that allows the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute to be removed from a route.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a BGP speaker is configured to remove the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute from a route, then this removal MUST be done prior to determining the degree of preference of the route and prior to performing route selection (Decision Process phases 1 and 2).
actions: remove MULTI_EXIT_DISC prior to determining degree of preference of the route
remove MULTI_EXIT_DISC prior to performing route selection (Decision Process phases 1 and 2)

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation MAY also (based on local configuration) alter the value of the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute received over EBGP.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a BGP speaker is configured to alter the value of the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute received over EBGP, then altering the value MUST be done prior to determining the degree of preference of the route and prior to performing route selection (Decision Process phases 1 and 2).
actions: alter MULTI_EXIT_DISC value prior to determining degree of preference of the route
alter MULTI_EXIT_DISC value prior to performing route selection (Decision Process phases 1 and 2)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: LOCAL_PREF is a well-known attribute that SHALL be included in all UPDATE messages that a given BGP speaker sends to other internal peers.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker SHALL calculate the degree of preference for each external route based on the locally-configured policy, and include the degree of preference when advertising a route to its internal peers.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The higher degree of preference MUST be preferred.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker MUST NOT include this attribute in UPDATE messages it sends to external peers, except in the case of BGP Confederations [RFC3065].

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If it is contained in an UPDATE message that is received from an external peer, then this attribute MUST be ignored by the receiving speaker, except in the case of BGP Confederations [RFC3065].

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If an aggregate excludes at least some of the AS numbers present in the AS_PATH of the routes that are aggregated as a result of dropping the AS_SET, the aggregated route, when advertised to the peer, SHOULD include the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute.
actions: include ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute in aggregated route advertisement sent to peer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker that receives a route with the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute SHOULD NOT remove the attribute when propagating the route to other speakers.
actions: retain ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute when propagating route to other BGP speakers

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker that receives a route with the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute MUST NOT make any NLRI of that route more specific (as defined in 9.1.4) when advertising this route to other BGP speakers.
actions: do not advertise any more-specific NLRI derived from a route carrying the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute

statements.subject: message
statements.description: AGGREGATOR is an optional transitive attribute, which MAY be included in updates that are formed by aggregation (see Section 9.2.2.2).

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker that performs route aggregation MAY add the AGGREGATOR attribute, which SHALL contain its own AS number and IP address.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The IP address SHOULD be the same as the BGP Identifier of the speaker.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If no Error Subcode is specified, then a zero MUST be used.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All errors detected while processing the Message Header MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Message Header Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Message Header Error

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the Marker field of the message header is not as expected, then a synchronization error has occurred and the Error Subcode MUST be set to Connection Not Synchronized.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Connection Not Synchronized

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad Message Length.
statements.pre_cond: (message.Length < 19 | message.Length > 4096) | (message.type = OPEN & message.Length < OPEN_min_length) | (message.type = UPDATE & message.Length < UPDATE_min_length) | (message.type = KEEPALIVE & message.Length != 19) | (message.type = NOTIFICATION & message.Length < NOTIFICATION_min_length)
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Bad Message Length

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the erroneous Length field.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the Type field of the message header is not recognized, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad Message Type.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Bad Message Type

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the erroneous Type field.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All errors detected while processing the OPEN message MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code OPEN Message Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION with Error Code = OPEN Message Error

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the version number in the Version field of the received OPEN message is not supported, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unsupported Version Number.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Unsupported Version Number

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the Autonomous System field of the OPEN message is unacceptable, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad Peer AS.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Bad Peer AS

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the Hold Time field of the OPEN message is unacceptable, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unacceptable Hold Time.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Unacceptable Hold Time

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation MUST reject Hold Time values of one or two seconds.
actions: reject the proposed Hold Time
set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Unacceptable Hold Time

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation MAY reject any proposed Hold Time.
actions: reject the proposed Hold Time

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: An implementation that accepts a Hold Time MUST use the negotiated value for the Hold Time.
actions: set Hold Time to the negotiated value from the OPEN message

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the BGP Identifier field of the OPEN message is syntactically incorrect, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Bad BGP Identifier.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Bad BGP Identifier

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If one of the Optional Parameters in the OPEN message is not recognized, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unsupported Optional Parameters.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = Unsupported Optional Parameters

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If one of the Optional Parameters in the OPEN message is recognized, but is malformed, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to 0 (Unspecific).
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode = 0 (Unspecific)

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All errors detected while processing the UPDATE message MUST be indicated by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code UPDATE Message Error.
actions: send NOTIFICATION message with Error Code=UPDATE Message Error

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the Withdrawn Routes Length or Total Attribute Length is too large (i.e., if Withdrawn Routes Length + Total Attribute Length + 23 exceeds the message Length), then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Malformed Attribute List.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Malformed Attribute List

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If any recognized attribute has Attribute Flags that conflict with the Attribute Type Code, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Attribute Flags Error.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Attribute Flags Error

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the erroneous attribute (type, length, and value).

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If any recognized attribute has an Attribute Length that conflicts with the expected length (based on the attribute type code), then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Attribute Length Error.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Attribute Length Error

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If any of the well-known mandatory attributes are not present, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Missing Well-known Attribute.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Missing Well-known Attribute

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the Attribute Type Code of the missing, well-known attribute.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If any of the well-known mandatory attributes are not recognized, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Unrecognized Well-known Attribute.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Unrecognized Well-known Attribute

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the unrecognized attribute (type, length, and value).

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the ORIGIN attribute has an undefined value, then the Error Sub-code MUST be set to Invalid Origin Attribute.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Invalid Origin Attribute

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the NEXT_HOP attribute field is syntactically incorrect, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Invalid NEXT_HOP Attribute.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Invalid NEXT_HOP Attribute

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the incorrect attribute (type, length, and value).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The IP address in the NEXT_HOP MUST meet the following criteria to be considered semantically correct:
actions: validate NEXT_HOP IP address against semantic correctness criteria

statements.subject: message
statements.description: a) It MUST NOT be the IP address of the receiving speaker.
actions: verify NEXT_HOP IP address is not equal to the receiving speaker's IP address

statements.subject: message
statements.description: b) In the case of an EBGP, where the sender and receiver are one IP hop away from each other, either the IP address in the NEXT_HOP MUST be the sender's IP address that is used to establish the BGP connection, or the interface associated with the NEXT_HOP IP address MUST share a common subnet with the receiving BGP speaker.
actions: verify NEXT_HOP is sender's BGP-connection IP address or shares a common subnet with the receiving BGP speaker

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the NEXT_HOP attribute is semantically incorrect, the error SHOULD be logged, and the route SHOULD be ignored.
actions: log the error
ignore the route

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In this case, a NOTIFICATION message SHOULD NOT be sent, and the connection SHOULD NOT be closed.
actions: do not send NOTIFICATION message
do not close the connection

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the path is syntactically incorrect, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Malformed AS_PATH.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Malformed AS_PATH

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the UPDATE message is received from an external peer, the local system MAY check whether the leftmost (with respect to the position of octets in the protocol message) AS in the AS_PATH attribute is equal to the autonomous system number of the peer that sent the message.
actions: optionally check that leftmost AS in AS_PATH equals the peer's autonomous system number

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the check determines this is not the case, the Error Subcode MUST be set to Malformed AS_PATH.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & peer.type = external & update_message.AS_PATH.leftmost_AS != peer.as_number
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Malformed AS_PATH

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If an optional attribute is recognized, then the value of this attribute MUST be checked.
actions: check the value of the recognized optional attribute

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If an error is detected, the attribute MUST be discarded, and the Error Subcode MUST be set to Optional Attribute Error.
actions: discard the erroneous optional attribute
set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Optional Attribute Error

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Data field MUST contain the attribute (type, length, and value).

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If any attribute appears more than once in the UPDATE message, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Malformed Attribute List.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Malformed Attribute List

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the field is syntactically incorrect, then the Error Subcode MUST be set to Invalid Network Field.
actions: set NOTIFICATION Error Subcode to Invalid Network Field

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a prefix in the NLRI field is semantically incorrect (e.g., an unexpected multicast IP address), an error SHOULD be logged locally, and the prefix SHOULD be ignored.
actions: log the error locally
ignore the semantically incorrect prefix

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An UPDATE message that contains correct path attributes, but no NLRI, SHALL be treated as a valid UPDATE message.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & update_message.path_attributes.correct = true & update_message.NLRI.present = false
actions: treat the UPDATE message as a valid UPDATE message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Any such error (e.g., an unrecognized Error Code or Error Subcode) SHOULD be noticed, logged locally, and brought to the attention of the administration of the peer.
actions: notice the error
log error locally
bring error to the attention of the administration of the peer

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: a BGP peer MAY choose, at any given time, to close its BGP connection by sending the NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease.
actions: Send NOTIFICATION message with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: message
statements.description: However, the Cease NOTIFICATION message MUST NOT be used when a fatal error indicated by this section does exist.
actions: Do not send NOTIFICATION with Error Code Cease

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker MAY support the ability to impose a locally-configured, upper bound on the number of address prefixes the speaker is willing to accept from a neighbor.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the BGP speaker decides to terminate its BGP connection with a neighbor because the number of address prefixes received from the neighbor exceeds the locally-configured, upper bound, then the speaker MUST send the neighbor a NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Cease.
actions: Send NOTIFICATION message with Error Code Cease to neighbor
Terminate BGP connection with neighbor

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The speaker MAY also log this locally.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In the event of connection collision, one of the connections MUST be closed.
actions: Close one of the two colliding BGP connections

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Upon receipt of an OPEN message, the local system MUST examine all of its connections that are in the OpenConfirm state.
actions: Examine all connections currently in OpenConfirm state for collision with the newly received OPEN message

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker MAY also examine connections in an OpenSent state if it knows the BGP Identifier of the peer by means outside of the protocol.
actions: Examine connections in OpenSent state for collision with the newly received OPEN message

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: BGP speakers MAY negotiate the version of the protocol by making multiple attempts at opening a BGP connection, starting with the highest version number each BGP speaker supports.
actions: attempt OPEN with highest supported BGP version
retry OPEN with lower version on Unsupported Version Number NOTIFICATION

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In order to support BGP version negotiation, future versions of BGP MUST retain the format of the OPEN and NOTIFICATION messages.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: These optional attributes may be supported, either per connection or per local system:

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Each event below has a name, definition, status (mandatory or optional), and the optional session attributes that SHOULD be set at each stage.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PassiveTcpEstablishment attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE.
actions: Set PassiveTcpEstablishment to FALSE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AllowAutomaticStart attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE if this event occurs.
actions: Set AllowAutomaticStart to TRUE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the PassiveTcpEstablishment optional session attribute is supported, it SHOULD be set to FALSE.
actions: Set PassiveTcpEstablishment to FALSE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the DampPeerOscillations is supported, it SHOULD be set to FALSE when this event occurs.
actions: Set DampPeerOscillations to FALSE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PassiveTcpEstablishment attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE if this event occurs.
actions: Set PassiveTcpEstablishment to TRUE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DampPeerOscillations attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE when this event occurs.
actions: Set DampPeerOscillations to FALSE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AllowAutomaticStart attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.
actions: Set AllowAutomaticStart to TRUE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PassiveTcpEstablishment attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.
actions: Set PassiveTcpEstablishment to TRUE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the DampPeerOscillations attribute is supported, the DampPeerOscillations SHOULD be set to FALSE.
actions: Set DampPeerOscillations to FALSE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DampPeerOscillations attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.
actions: Set DampPeerOscillations to TRUE

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AllowAutomaticStop attribute SHOULD be TRUE.
actions: Set AllowAutomaticStop to TRUE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: DelayOpen attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE,
actions: set DelayOpen attribute to TRUE

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: DelayOpenTime attribute SHOULD be supported,
actions: support DelayOpenTime attribute

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: DelayOpenTimer SHOULD be supported.
actions: support DelayOpenTimer

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: Implementations not implementing the persistent peer oscillation damping function may not have the IdleHoldTimer.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: DampPeerOscillations attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.
actions: set DampPeerOscillations attribute to TRUE

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: IdleHoldTimer SHOULD have just expired.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: BGP's destination port SHOULD be port 179, as defined by IANA.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: The TrackTcpState attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE if this event occurs.
actions: Set TrackTcpState to TRUE

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: BGP destination port number SHOULD be 179, as defined by IANA.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The DelayOpen optional attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD not be running.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The DelayOpen attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD be running.

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: CollisionDetectEstablishedState optional attribute SHOULD be set to TRUE.
actions: set CollisionDetectEstablishedState to TRUE

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: BGP MUST maintain a separate FSM for each configured peer.
actions: Instantiate and maintain a separate FSM for each configured peer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP implementation MUST connect to and listen on TCP port 179 for incoming connections in addition to trying to connect to peers.
actions: Listen on TCP port 179 for incoming connections
Attempt outgoing TCP connections to configured peers

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: For each incoming connection, a state machine MUST be instantiated.
actions: Instantiate a new FSM for the incoming TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: During this time, both an incoming and outgoing connection may exist for the same configured peering.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: There may be more than one connection between a pair of peers if the connections are configured to use a different pair of IP addresses.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When a BGP speaker is configured as active, it may end up on either the active or passive side of the connection that eventually gets established.
actions: Accept active or passive side of the established TCP connection regardless of configured role

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: After the connection collision is resolved (see Section 6.8), the FSM for the connection that is closed SHOULD be disposed.
actions: dispose FSM associated with the closed connection

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: For optional attributes that act as flags, if the optional session attribute can be set to TRUE on the system, the corresponding BGP FSM actions must be supported.
actions: Support all BGP FSM actions corresponding to the optional session attribute

statements.subject: state_machine
statements.description: For example, if the following options can be set in a BGP implementation: AutoStart and PassiveTcpEstablishment, then Events 3, 4 and 5 must be supported.
statements.post_cond: Event3.supported = true & Event4.supported = true & Event5.supported = true
actions: Support Event 3
Support Event 4
Support Event 5

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Implementations MAY use these numbers to provide network management information.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The exact value of the ConnectRetryTimer is a local matter, but it SHOULD be sufficiently large to allow TCP initialization.
actions: Set ConnectRetryTimer initial value to a duration sufficiently large to allow TCP initialization

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: In response to an indication that the TCP connection is successfully established (Event 16 or Event 17), the second connection SHALL be tracked until it sends an OPEN message.
actions: Track second TCP connection until it sends an OPEN message

statements.subject: message
statements.description: An UPDATE message may be received only in the Established state.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the UPDATE message contains a non-empty WITHDRAWN ROUTES field, the previously advertised routes, whose destinations (expressed as IP prefixes) are contained in this field, SHALL be removed from the Adj-RIB-In.
actions: Remove previously advertised routes listed in WITHDRAWN ROUTES field from Adj-RIB-In

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: This BGP speaker SHALL run its Decision Process because the previously advertised route is no longer available for use.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & UPDATE.WITHDRAWN_ROUTES != empty & Adj-RIB-In.routes_removed = true
actions: Run Decision Process

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the UPDATE message contains a feasible route, the Adj-RIB-In will be updated with this route as follows: if the NLRI of the new route is identical to the one the route currently has stored in the Adj-RIB-In, then the new route SHALL replace the older route in the Adj-RIB-In, thus implicitly withdrawing the older route from service.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & UPDATE.feasible_route = true & Adj-RIB-In.existing_route.NLRI = new_route.NLRI
actions: Replace older route in Adj-RIB-In with new route
Implicitly withdraw older route from service

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Otherwise, if the Adj-RIB-In has no route with NLRI identical to the new route, the new route SHALL be placed in the Adj-RIB-In.
actions: Place new route in Adj-RIB-In

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Once the BGP speaker updates the Adj-RIB-In, the speaker SHALL run its Decision Process.
actions: Run Decision Process

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The function that calculates the degree of preference for a given route SHALL NOT use any of the following as its inputs: the existence of other routes, the non-existence of other routes, or the path attributes of other routes.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the return value indicates the route is ineligible, the route MAY NOT serve as an input to the next phase of route selection; otherwise, the return value MUST be used as the LOCAL_PREF value in any IBGP readvertisement.
actions: exclude route from Phase 2 route selection input

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the NEXT_HOP attribute of a BGP route depicts an address that is not resolvable, or if it would become unresolvable if the route was installed in the routing table, the BGP route MUST be excluded from the Phase 2 decision function.
actions: exclude BGP route from Phase 2 decision function

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the AS_PATH attribute of a BGP route contains an AS loop, the BGP route should be excluded from the Phase 2 decision function.
actions: exclude BGP route from Phase 2 decision function

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The local speaker SHALL then install that route in the Loc-RIB, replacing any route to the same destination that is currently being held in the Loc-RIB.
actions: install selected route in Loc-RIB
replace existing route to same destination currently held in Loc-RIB

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When the new BGP route is installed in the Routing Table, care must be taken to ensure that existing routes to the same destination that are now considered invalid are removed from the Routing Table.
actions: remove from Routing Table all existing routes to same destination now considered invalid

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The local speaker MUST determine the immediate next-hop address from the NEXT_HOP attribute of the selected route (see Section 5.1.3).
actions: determine immediate next-hop address from NEXT_HOP attribute of selected route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If either the immediate next-hop or the IGP cost to the NEXT_HOP (where the NEXT_HOP is resolved through an IGP route) changes, Phase 2 Route Selection MUST be performed again.
actions: re-invoke Phase 2 Route Selection

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Notice that even though BGP routes do not have to be installed in the Routing Table with the immediate next-hop(s), implementations MUST take care that, before any packets are forwarded along a BGP route, its associated NEXT_HOP address is resolved to the immediate (directly connected) next-hop address, and that this address (or multiple addresses) is finally used for actual packet forwarding.
actions: resolve NEXT_HOP to immediate (directly connected) next-hop address before forwarding any packet along BGP route
use resolved immediate next-hop address for actual packet forwarding

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Unresolvable routes SHALL be removed from the Loc-RIB and the routing table.
actions: remove unresolvable routes from Loc-RIB
remove unresolvable routes from routing table

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: However, corresponding unresolvable routes SHOULD be kept in the Adj-RIBs-In (in case they become resolvable).
actions: retain unresolvable routes in Adj-RIBs-In

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: As indicated in Section 9.1.2, BGP speakers SHOULD exclude unresolvable routes from the Phase 2 decision.
actions: exclude unresolvable routes from Phase 2 decision

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If multiple matching routes are available, only the longest matching route SHOULD be considered.
actions: consider only the longest matching route for resolvability

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Whenever a BGP speaker identifies a route that fails the resolvability check because of mutual recursion, an error message SHOULD be logged.
actions: log error message identifying the mutually recursive route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The criteria MUST be applied in the order specified.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: BGP implementations MAY use any algorithm that produces the same results as those described here.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute is removed before re-advertising a route into IBGP, then comparison based on the received EBGP MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute MAY still be performed.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If an implementation chooses to remove MULTI_EXIT_DISC, then the optional comparison on MULTI_EXIT_DISC, if performed, MUST be performed only among EBGP-learned routes.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: For IBGP-learned routes, the MULTI_EXIT_DISC MUST be used in route comparisons that reach this step in the Decision Process.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: This policy MAY exclude a route in the Loc-RIB from being installed in a particular Adj-RIB-Out.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A route SHALL NOT be installed in the Adj-Rib-Out unless the destination, and NEXT_HOP described by this route, may be forwarded appropriately by the Routing Table.
actions: reject installation of route into Adj-RIB-Out

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a route in Loc-RIB is excluded from a particular Adj-RIB-Out, the previously advertised route in that Adj-RIB-Out MUST be withdrawn from service by means of an UPDATE message (see 9.2).
actions: send UPDATE message withdrawing previously advertised route from Adj-RIB-Out

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Route aggregation and information reduction techniques (see Section 9.2.2.1) may optionally be applied.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker may transmit routes with overlapping Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) to another BGP speaker.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a BGP speaker receives overlapping routes, the Decision Process MUST consider both routes based on the configured acceptance policy.
actions: Consider both routes based on configured acceptance policy

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If both a less and a more specific route are accepted, then the Decision Process MUST install, in Loc-RIB, either both the less and the more specific routes or aggregate the two routes and install, in Loc-RIB, the aggregated route, provided that both routes have the same value of the NEXT_HOP attribute.
statements.pre_cond: route.less_specific.accepted = true & route.more_specific.accepted = true & route.less_specific.NEXT_HOP = route.more_specific.NEXT_HOP
actions: Install both less-specific and more-specific routes in Loc-RIB OR aggregate the two routes and install aggregated route in Loc-RIB

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If a BGP speaker chooses to aggregate, then it SHOULD either include all ASes used to form the aggregate in an AS_SET, or add the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute to the route.
actions: Include all ASes used to form the aggregate in an AS_SET OR add ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute to the route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Routes SHOULD NOT be de-aggregated.
actions: Do not de-aggregate routes

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In particular, a route that carries the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute MUST NOT be de-aggregated.
actions: Do not de-aggregate a route carrying the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: the receiving BGP speaker SHALL NOT re-distribute the routing information contained in that UPDATE message to other internal peers (unless the speaker acts as a BGP Route Reflector [RFC2796]).
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & message.source = internal_peer & speaker.role != Route_Reflector
actions: suppress redistribution of routing information from UPDATE to other internal peers

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: All newly installed routes and all newly unfeasible routes for which there is no replacement route SHALL be advertised to its peers by means of an UPDATE message.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Established & (route.newly_installed = true | (route.newly_unfeasible = true & route.replacement_exists = false))
actions: advertise newly installed routes to peers via UPDATE message
advertise newly unfeasible routes with no replacement to peers via UPDATE message

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP speaker SHOULD NOT advertise a given feasible BGP route from its Adj-RIB-Out if it would produce an UPDATE message containing the same BGP route as was previously advertised.
actions: suppress advertisement of route that would produce a duplicate UPDATE message

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Any routes in the Loc-RIB marked as unfeasible SHALL be removed.
actions: remove unfeasible routes from Loc-RIB

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Changes to the reachable destinations within its own autonomous system SHALL also be advertised in an UPDATE message.
actions: advertise changes to reachable destinations within own AS via UPDATE message

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If, due to the limits on the maximum size of an UPDATE message (see Section 4), a single route doesn't fit into the message, the BGP speaker MUST not advertise the route to its peers and MAY choose to log an error locally.
actions: do not advertise the oversized route to peers

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Two UPDATE messages sent by a BGP speaker to a peer that advertise feasible routes and/or withdrawal of unfeasible routes to some common set of destinations MUST be separated by at least MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer.
actions: Enforce minimum interval of MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer between consecutive UPDATE messages to same peer covering overlapping destinations

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Since fast convergence is needed within an autonomous system, either (a) the MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer used for internal peers SHOULD be shorter than the MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer used for external peers, or (b) the procedure describe in this section SHOULD NOT apply to routes sent to internal peers.
actions: Configure MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer for internal peers to be shorter than for external peers

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If new routes are selected multiple times while awaiting the expiration of MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer, the last route selected SHALL be advertised at the end of MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer.
actions: Advertise the most recently selected route to peer upon expiration of MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Having selected the routing information it will advertise, a BGP speaker may avail itself of several methods to organize this information in an efficient manner.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The Decision Process may optionally reduce the amount of information that it will place in the Adj-RIBs-Out by any of the following methods:

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: their use may prune potentially feasible paths because such paths are no longer listed individually in the form of AS_SEQUENCEs.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Routes that have different MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes SHALL NOT be aggregated.
actions: do not aggregate routes that have different MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the aggregated route has an AS_SET as the first element in its AS_PATH attribute, then the router that originates the route SHOULD NOT advertise the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute with this route.
actions: do not advertise MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute with the aggregated route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Path attributes of the same type code may be aggregated, according to the following rules:

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When aggregating routes that have different NEXT_HOP attributes, the NEXT_HOP attribute of the aggregated route SHALL identify an interface on the BGP speaker that performs the aggregation.
actions: set NEXT_HOP attribute of aggregated route to an interface on the BGP speaker performing aggregation

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If at least one route among routes that are aggregated has ORIGIN with the value INCOMPLETE, then the aggregated route MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value INCOMPLETE.
actions: set ORIGIN attribute of aggregated route to INCOMPLETE

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Otherwise, if at least one route among routes that are aggregated has ORIGIN with the value EGP, then the aggregated route MUST have the ORIGIN attribute with the value EGP.
statements.pre_cond: !exists(route in routes_to_aggregate: route.ORIGIN = INCOMPLETE) & exists(route in routes_to_aggregate: route.ORIGIN = EGP)
actions: set ORIGIN attribute of aggregated route to EGP

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the routes to be aggregated have different AS_PATH attributes, then the aggregated AS_PATH attribute SHALL satisfy all of the following conditions:
actions: ensure aggregated AS_PATH attribute satisfies all specified conditions

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: all tuples of type AS_SEQUENCE in the aggregated AS_PATH SHALL appear in all of the AS_PATHs in the initial set of routes to be aggregated.
statements.post_cond: forall(t in aggregated_AS_PATH: t.type = AS_SEQUENCE => forall(p in initial_AS_PATHs: t in p))
actions: include in aggregated AS_PATH only AS_SEQUENCE tuples present in every initial AS_PATH

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: all tuples of type AS_SET in the aggregated AS_PATH SHALL appear in at least one of the AS_PATHs in the initial set (they may appear as either AS_SET or AS_SEQUENCE types).
statements.post_cond: forall(t in aggregated_AS_PATH: t.type = AS_SET => exists(p in initial_AS_PATHs: t.value in p))
actions: include in aggregated AS_PATH only AS_SET tuples whose value appears in at least one initial AS_PATH

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: No tuple of type AS_SET with the same value SHALL appear more than once in the aggregated AS_PATH.
actions: eliminate duplicate AS_SET tuples with the same value from the aggregated AS_PATH

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Multiple tuples of type AS_SEQUENCE with the same value may appear in the aggregated AS_PATH only when adjacent to another tuple of the same type and value.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation may choose any algorithm that conforms to these rules.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: At a minimum, a conformant implementation SHALL be able to perform the following algorithm that meets all of the above conditions:
actions: implement at minimum the specified AS_PATH aggregation algorithm

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If at least one of the routes to be aggregated has ATOMIC_AGGREGATE path attribute, then the aggregated route SHALL have this attribute as well.
actions: include ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute in the aggregated route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Any AGGREGATOR attributes from the routes to be aggregated MUST NOT be included in the aggregated route.
actions: exclude all AGGREGATOR attributes inherited from routes to be aggregated from the aggregated route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The BGP speaker performing the route aggregation MAY attach a new AGGREGATOR attribute (see Section 5.1.7).
actions: optionally attach a new AGGREGATOR attribute to the aggregated route

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Thus, an AS SHOULD avoid using unstable routes, and it SHOULD NOT make rapid, spontaneous changes to its choice of route.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: These routes MAY also be distributed to other BGP speakers within the local AS as part of the update process (see Section 9.2).

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The decision of whether to distribute non-BGP acquired routes within an AS via BGP depends on the environment within the AS (e.g., type of IGP) and SHOULD be controlled via configuration.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Two optional timers MAY be supported: DelayOpenTimer, IdleHoldTimer by BGP (see Section 8).
actions: optionally support DelayOpenTimer
optionally support IdleHoldTimer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation of BGP MUST allow the HoldTimer to be configurable on a per-peer basis, and MAY allow the other timers to be configurable.
actions: allow HoldTimer to be configurable on a per-peer basis
optionally allow ConnectRetryTimer, KeepaliveTimer, and other timers to be configurable

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: To minimize the likelihood that the distribution of BGP messages by a given BGP speaker will contain peaks, jitter SHOULD be applied to the timers associated with MinASOriginationIntervalTimer, KeepaliveTimer, MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer, and ConnectRetryTimer.
statements.post_cond: MinASOriginationIntervalTimer.jitter_applied = true & KeepaliveTimer.jitter_applied = true & MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer.jitter_applied = true & ConnectRetryTimer.jitter_applied = true
actions: apply jitter to MinASOriginationIntervalTimer
apply jitter to KeepaliveTimer
apply jitter to MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer
apply jitter to ConnectRetryTimer

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A given BGP speaker MAY apply the same jitter to each of these quantities, regardless of the destinations to which the updates are being sent; that is, jitter need not be configured on a per-peer basis.
actions: optionally apply a single uniform jitter value across all peers rather than per-peer jitter

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The suggested default amount of jitter SHALL be determined by multiplying the base value of the appropriate timer by a random factor, which is uniformly distributed in the range from 0.75 to 1.0.
actions: compute timer jitter value as timer.base_value multiplied by a random factor uniformly distributed in [0.75, 1.0]

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: A new random value SHOULD be picked each time the timer is set.
actions: select a new random jitter factor each time the timer is set

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The range of the jitter's random value MAY be configurable.
actions: optionally expose the jitter random value range as a configurable parameter

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Implementations MUST support TCP MD5 [RFC2385] for authentication.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a local system TCP user interface supports the TCP PUSH function, then each BGP message SHOULD be transmitted with PUSH flag set.
actions: Set PUSH flag on each outgoing BGP message

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a local system TCP user interface supports setting the DSCP field [RFC2474] for TCP connections, then the TCP connection used by BGP SHOULD be opened with bits 0-2 of the DSCP field set to 110 (binary).
actions: Open TCP connection with DSCP field bits 0-2 set to 110 (binary)

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation MUST support the TCP MD5 option [RFC2385].

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Using this capability is highly recommended.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: When peering with a BGP implementation that does not compress multiple address prefixes into one message, it may be necessary to take steps to reduce the overhead from the flood of data received when a peer is acquired or when a significant network topology change occurs.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: By choosing a minimum flash update interval that is not much greater than the time it takes to process the multiple messages, this latency should be minimized.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: To avoid excessive route flapping, a BGP speaker that needs to withdraw a destination and send an update about a more specific or less specific route should combine them into the same UPDATE message.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Implementations that combine update messages (as described above in Section 6.1) may prefer to see all path attributes presented in a known order.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: This optimization is entirely optional.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Because BGP-4 is capable of carrying aggregated routes that cannot be properly represented in BGP-3, an implementation that supports BGP-4 and another BGP version should provide the capability to only speak BGP-4 on a per-peer basis.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: An implementation that chooses to provide a path aggregation algorithm retaining significant amounts of path information may wish to use the following procedure:

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If, as a result of the above procedure, a given AS number appears more than once within the aggregated AS_PATH attribute, all but the last instance (rightmost occurrence) of that AS number should be removed from the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A BGP implementation MUST support the authentication mechanism specified in RFC 2385 [RFC2385].

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: A compliant implementation must support this mechanism, and must allow a network administrator to activate it on a per-peer basis.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: It notes that a distinct key should be used for communication with each protected peer.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: If the same key is used for multiple peers, the offered security services may be degraded, e.g., due to an increased risk of compromise at one router that adversely affects other routers.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: The keys used for MAC computation should be changed periodically, to minimize the impact of a key compromise or successful cryptanalytic attack.

statements.subject: bgp
statements.description: Obviously, each should key also be chosen to be difficult for an attacker to guess.
